frames.narration: Train a 70B model on 64 GPUs of 80 GB. Mixed-precision Adam needs about 16 bytes per parameter: 70 x 16 = 1,120 GB of state, before activations. One GPU cannot hold it.
Data parallel: every replica sees different data, then the gradients must be averaged. Replicating the full state would still cost 1,120 GB per GPU, so this alone does not fit.
Shard it (ZeRO-3 / FSDP): each of 64 GPUs keeps 1/64 of the state, 17.5 GB. Layers are all-gathered just in time and gradients reduce-scattered, about 1.5x the traffic of plain data parallel.
Tensor parallel splits each layer across the 8 GPUs of a node. It needs all-reduces in every layer, so it stays on the fast links inside the node.
Pipeline parallel gives node A the first layers and node B the last, passing activations over the network. With 8 stages and 8 microbatches, 7/15 = 47% of the time is bubble.
More microbatches fill the pipeline: with 64 microbatches the bubble falls to 7/71, about 10%. Utilisation (MFU) is what you track: useful FLOPs over peak.
Every 30 minutes the workers write their shards to storage. 14 bytes per parameter is about 980 GB, written in about 20 s.
At 4,096 GPUs a failure happens about every 12 hours. Node B dies mid-step; the synchronous job cannot continue, and the controller stops everyone.
A spare node joins and all workers reload the last checkpoint. The work since that save, up to 30 minutes, plus restart time is lost. This is the interval trade-off.
